newsitem.title: UK: Cambodia hit by intimidation and arrests - Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia hit by intimidation and arrests - Amnesty.

text.p: Amnesty International on Tuesday accused Cambodian forces loyal to Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of conducting a violent campaign of intimidation, arrests and harassment of politicians, party activists and journalists.

More than 50 people are currently in hiding or in need of protection in Cambodia, scene of bitter fighting in recent days. The fate and whereabouts of 13 people detained in Battambang province and 22 in Prey Veng is unknown, Amnesty said.

Pierre Sane, secretary general of the London-based human rights organisation, called on the international community to provide protection to anyone seeking asylum and on governments, particularly in Asia, to put "the strongest pressure possible" on those controlling Cambodia to ensure the safety of detainees.

"The last three days have seen systematic targeting of key members of FUNCINPEC, clearly aimed at cowing opposition to Hun Sen's party and instilling a climate of fear throughout the country," Sane said in a statement.
Hun Sen toppled First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, head of the FUNCINPEC party, at the weekend.
"The Cambodian authorities should provide details of the numbers and names of those in detention, details of any charges against them and assurances that they will not be ill-treated," Sane said.

"A durable political settlement to the current crisis will be impossible without safeguards for human rights." Amnesty said it was gravely concerned at reports that Ho Sok, a senior FUNCINPEC official, had been shot and killed.
